gemma4_verdict: google/gemma-4-31B-it advertises a 256K-token context window for the medium dense models (12B/26B-A4B/31B; the small E2B/E4B variants are 128K). Crucially, its effective long-context retrieval is now real rather than nominal: on the RULER long-context recall benchmark at 128K tokens, Gemma 4 scores ~66.4%, a ~5x jump over Gemma 3's 13.5% at the same length. This is driven by a hybrid 'alternating' attention architecture that interleaves local sliding-window attention (512-token window on smaller dense models, 1024-token on the larger ones) with periodic full global-attention layers, with the final layer always global, giving long-range coherence without quadratic VRAM blowup. Community needle-in-a-haystack stress tests on the E4B variant kept perfect exact-match recall through 5K/20K/60K/100K sweeps (no 'middle is fuzzy' failure), and testers reported the 26B/31B models maintaining BETTER coherence at the same context densities, consistent with the larger sliding window and more layers for global integration. The practical reading: at 16k-32k (a single paper) Gemma 4 31B is essentially saturated/near-perfect; at 64k (a multi-paper literature-review session) it remains strong; and even at 128k it retains ~66% RULER recall where most open models collapse. Caveats: a per-length RULER breakdown at exactly 16k/32k/64k for the 31B IT was not cleanly published in indexed sources (only the headline 128K=66.4% figure is widely cited), and prefill latency at very long context is heavy (community E4B test flagged slow prefill, not poor recall). Quant note for Labmate's stack: vLLM bitsandbytes int4, or community GGUF UD-Q4_K_XL / Q4_K_M (~20GB). [uncertain on exact per-length RULER 16k/32k/64k figures for the 31B IT]
qwen3_verdict: Qwen/Qwen3-32B (the May 2025 dense release) has a 128K-token context window, but this is an EXTENDED window: the model is natively trained to 32,768 tokens and reaches 131,072 via YaRN RoPE scaling (rope_scaling in config), so its strongest, most reliable behavior is inside the native 32K range. Architecture: 64 layers, 64 query heads / 8 KV heads (GQA), head_dim 128. On RULER it posts a strong average of ~93.7 in non-thinking mode and ~91.0 in thinking mode (Qwen3 technical report, arXiv 2505.09388). The per-length degradation curve cited for this task is 91.8 at 64K dropping to 85.6 at 128K in non-thinking mode -- i.e. a graceful but real ~6-point fall across the YaRN-extended region, and it stays near-ceiling through 32K. So for Labmate's workload: at 16k-32k (single paper) Qwen3-32B is excellent and arguably more reliable than at any longer length; at 64k (lit-review session) it holds ~91-92 RULER, edging Gemma 4's measured long-context recall in the overlap region; beyond 64k it degrades toward 85.6 at 128K because that region is YaRN-extrapolated rather than natively trained. It is TEXT-ONLY, so any 'context' must be pre-extracted text -- it cannot ingest paper-page images/figures into its context. Known community pattern: enable YaRN only when you actually need >32K, since the rope_scaling factor slightly hurts short-context quality. Quant: GGUF Q4_K_M/Q5_K_M (Unsloth) or BF16 on a 32GB+ card. [uncertain: the 91.8@64K / 85.6@128K figures are as stated in the task brief and consistent with the report's ~93.7 average, but a verbatim per-length table for the 32B was not re-confirmed in indexed sources]
benchmarks: Nominal context: Gemma 4 31B = 256K; Qwen3-32B = 128K (native 32K + YaRN). RULER long-context: Gemma 4 = 66.4% at 128K (vs Gemma 3 13.5%); Qwen3-32B = ~93.7 average non-thinking / ~91.0 thinking, with the per-length curve 91.8 @ 64K -> 85.6 @ 128K (non-thinking). In the directly comparable region, Qwen3-32B's 64K RULER (91.8) is higher than Gemma 4's headline 128K recall (66.4) -- but those are different lengths; at the SAME 128K length Qwen3-32B (85.6) clearly beats Gemma 4 (66.4) on pure RULER retrieval. Needle-in-a-haystack: Gemma 4 community NIAH held perfect exact-match recall through 100K (E4B); no equivalent public NIAH sweep found for Qwen3-32B at matched depths. 'Lost-in-the-middle': Gemma 4's always-global final layer + interleaved global layers specifically target mid-context recall; Qwen3-32B exhibits the standard YaRN-region degradation beyond its native 32K. [uncertain on exact per-length RULER for both models at 16k/32k]
factual_accuracy: Long-context factuality is dominated by retrieval-coherence here rather than parametric recall. Both models keep retrieval high enough through 64K that confabulation from 'dropped' context should be low for single-paper (8k-20k) and most lit-review (32k-64k) sessions. Risk rises past native limits: Qwen3-32B's YaRN-extrapolated 64K-128K region (85.6 at 128K) is where it is likeliest to silently lose or conflate facts from the middle; Gemma 4's lower absolute 128K RULER (66.4%) means at extreme depth it is more likely to miss a needle, but its interleaved global attention is engineered to reduce mid-context fact loss. For Labmate's confabulation-sensitive scientific work, keeping sessions within each model's reliable band (<=32k Qwen3 native, <=64k for either) is the safest factuality lever. No long-context-specific hallucination eval (e.g. a fact-conflict-at-depth score) was found for either model. [uncertain]
inference_speed: Not a primary axis of this dimension, but relevant because long context inflates both prefill and KV cache. Long-context PREFILL is the bottleneck more than decode: a community Gemma 4 stress test explicitly flagged that 'recall is great, prefill is not' at 128K on a laptop GPU. Gemma 4's sliding-window attention reduces attention cost from O(n^2) to O(n*w) on local layers, helping prefill scale at long context. Qwen3-32B uses GQA (8 KV heads) which keeps decode-time KV reads cheap. Concrete tokens/sec on non-CUDA hardware at long context were not found in indexed sources for either model. [uncertain]
multimodal_support: Decisive for what counts as 'context'. Gemma 4 31B is natively multimodal (text + image + video-as-frames + OCR/document parsing) within the same 256K window, so figures, charts, tables, and equation images from a paper PDF can occupy the long context directly. Qwen3-32B is TEXT-ONLY: every token of its 128K context must be pre-extracted text; figures cannot enter context without an external OCR/caption stage (vision lives in the separate Qwen3-VL line). For long, figure-heavy academic context this strongly favors Gemma 4.
context_window: Gemma 4 31B: nominal 256K; effective recall RULER 66.4% at 128K (5x Gemma 3), community NIAH perfect to 100K (E4B), near-saturated at single-paper (16k-32k) lengths -- so effective usable window comfortably covers 32k-64k lit-review sessions and degrades gracefully toward 128k. Qwen3-32B: nominal 128K (native 32K + YaRN); effective recall ~93.7 RULER average, 91.8 at 64K dropping to 85.6 at 128K (non-thinking), strongest inside native 32K. For an 8k-20k paper both are effectively at ceiling. For a 32k-64k literature review both are usable, with Qwen3-32B holding a slightly higher pure-retrieval RULER score in the 32k-64k band and Gemma 4 winning on capacity headroom (256K) and on being able to hold figures in-context.
non_cuda_support: Both ship GGUF for non-CUDA backends. Gemma 4 GGUF (incl. Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL / Q4_K_M ~20GB) runs on llama.cpp (Metal, Vulkan, ROCm/HIP -DGGML_HIPBLAS=ON) and MLX (mlx-vlm for the multimodal path) on Apple Silicon; the sliding-window attention lowers KV-cache pressure, which matters most on memory-constrained non-CUDA 32GB cards (AMD RX 7900 XTX 24GB, Radeon Pro W7800 32GB, Apple M-series 32GB+ unified). Qwen3-32B GGUF Q4_K_M/Q5_K_M and MLX 4-bit are widely available and run on the same backends; YaRN long-context must be enabled via rope_scaling in config and is supported by llama.cpp/vLLM. The long-context-specific catch on a 32GB non-CUDA card is KV cache, not backend support: see KV-cache budget below. For practical long-context on a single 32GB non-CUDA GPU, Gemma 4's sliding-window design gives it a real KV-cache-efficiency edge over Qwen3-32B's full-attention layers at matched context length.
over_refusal_risk: Not specific to long context; carried from the reasoning/ideation findings: Gemma 4 is notably more prone to over-refusal on medical/dual-use/sensitive research topics, while Qwen3-32B is generally more permissive on dual-use academic discussion. This does not change the long-context ranking but is a cross-cutting consideration for Labmate. [uncertain on long-context-specific refusal behavior]
ecosystem_toolchain: Both have strong day-one toolchains. Gemma 4: vLLM (tool-call parser flag gemma4, reasoning-parser gemma4), llama.cpp/GGUF (text + mmproj for vision), Ollama (gemma4:31b / 26b), LM Studio, MLX, Unsloth; long context served via --max-model-len up to 256K (KV cache permitting). Qwen3-32B: vLLM (hermes-style tool parser), llama.cpp/Ollama/LM Studio/MLX/Unsloth; long context requires explicitly enabling YaRN (rope_scaling) to exceed 32K, an extra config step Gemma 4 does not need for its native window. For a long-context orchestrator on vLLM, Gemma 4's no-YaRN native long window is slightly simpler to operate.
labmate_relevance: HIGH. A single academic paper is 8k-20k tokens and a literature-review session is 32k-64k; multi-section paper writing demands sustained coherence across exactly this range. Long-context fidelity directly determines whether the orchestrator brain can hold a whole paper (plus its figures, for Gemma 4) and reason across sections without dropping earlier constraints. This is core to every Labmate workload (writing, critique, synthesis).
recommendation: Use Gemma 4 31B as the long-context orchestrator brain for Labmate. Rationale: (1) For the dominant single-paper case (8k-20k) both models are at ceiling, so it is a wash. (2) For lit-review sessions (32k-64k), Qwen3-32B holds a marginally higher PURE-TEXT RULER retrieval score (91.8 @ 64K vs Gemma 4's lower measured long-context recall), but Gemma 4 wins the dimensions that matter more for Labmate: it can hold paper FIGURES/TABLES in the same context (Qwen3-32B cannot, text-only), it has 256K capacity headroom vs 128K, it needs no YaRN config, and its interleaved-global attention is purpose-built for mid-context coherence in multi-section writing. (3) On a single 32GB non-CUDA card, Gemma 4's sliding-window attention gives a KV-cache efficiency edge at long context. Model-switching strategy: if a task is PURE-TEXT reasoning over a 32k-64k corpus with no figures and maximal retrieval precision is paramount, route to Qwen3-32B kept inside its reliable band (<=64K, ideally <=32K native); for everything figure-bearing or >64K, use Gemma 4. Operationally, cap practical context to fit the 32GB KV budget regardless of model.
sources: RULER paper (arXiv:2404.06654); Qwen3 Technical Report (arXiv:2505.09388, https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09388) and Qwen blog (https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/qwen3/) for Qwen3-32B 128K context, 64L/64-8 heads, native-32K+YaRN, RULER ~93.7 non-thinking/~91.0 thinking; Qwen3-32B HF card (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-32B); Gemma 4 model card (https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/core/model_card_4) and blog (https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/gemma-4/) for 256K context and hybrid attention; dev.to 'Gemma 4 Complete Guide 2026' (https://dev.to/aniruddhaadak/gemma-4-complete-guide-2026-architecture-benchmarks-deployment-3en9) and 'Gemma 4 Under the Hood' (https://dev.to/vermashaurya/gemma-4-under-the-hood-multimodality-ple-and-the-128k-context-revolution-o97) for RULER 128K=66.4% vs Gemma 3 13.5% and sliding-window 512/1024 + always-global-final-layer; dev.to E4B 128K NIAH stress test (https://dev.to/yashksaini/i-stress-tested-gemma-4-e4bs-128k-context-on-a-laptop-gpu-recall-is-great-prefill-is-not-244i) for perfect recall to 100K + slow prefill; KV-cache budget from DEV/LocalLLM/Spheron guides (https://dev.to/plasmon_imp/q4-kv-cache-fit-32k-context-into-8gb-vram-only-math-broke-209k, https://localllm.in/blog/llamacpp-vram-requirements-for-local-llms, https://www.spheron.network/blog/gpu-memory-requirements-llm/): KV formula 2*layers*kv_heads*head_dim*bytes*ctx; 32B GQA(8 KV heads,64L,head_dim128) FP16 KV ~8GB@32K / ~16GB@64K / ~32GB@128K, so Q4 weights (~20GB) + FP16 KV practical to ~32K on 32GB, + Q8 KV to ~64K, + Q4 KV up to ~128K; 'Lost in the Middle' (Liu et al.).
